title: Compact Orbit Handoff & Wayfinding: Workspace switcher + sidebar compression IA
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: The current Console sidebar and workspace switching patterns are dense and inconsistent across dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Users report friction when switching workspaces and when trying to locate rollout controls and per-route cost lenses. Goal: Produce a compact, low-visual-noise information architecture that groups routes by task-context, exposes workspace switching as a lightweight in-rail affordance, and surfaces rollout/cost lenses with progressive disclosure. Deliverables: (1) Updated IA diagram and route taxonomy, (2) high-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop (collapsed & expanded sidebar), (3) interactive microflow for workspace-switcher keyboard + click journeys, (4) usability test report (10 participants), (5) engineering handoff including component spec and telemetry events.
acceptance_criteria: IA diagram that reduces top-level sidebar items by >=30% via grouping and collapsible lanes
Collapsed-sidebar interaction preserves primary route discoverability within 2 clicks for 95% of tested tasks
Workspace switcher reachable in <=2 keyboard interactions (Cmd/Ctrl+K exempt) in prototype
Rollouts and cost lenses are discoverable from dashboard context menu with clear affordance and tooltip
Design tokens and spacing documented; component spec includes collapsed width, hover states, and focus rings
Telemetry spec with 15 event names (open_sidebar, toggle_workspace, open_rollout_panel, expand_cost_lens, etc.) provided for eng
decision_log: 2026-02-15 — Decided to shift from a full flyout workspace switcher to an in-rail micro-switcher to reduce visual context switching — agreed by PM (Diego Ramos) and Eng lead (Maya Patel)
2026-02-19 — Chose icon-letter condensed labels in collapsed state versus icon-only (accessibility readout for screen readers) — rationale: discoverability for new users
2026-02-27 — Deferred multi-tenant role-aware switcher to a follow-up since requirements require backend RBAC mapping (dependency ENG-4201)
comments: 2026-02-14 Priya Shah: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma. Key tension: balancing compactness with rollouts visibility. Added four variant flows (rail-compact, rail-micro, flyout, command-palette-first).
2026-02-18 Diego Ramos (PM): Prefer the micro-switcher variant, aligns with PLG onboarding flow. Request: show recent 3 workspaces and a pinned list.
2026-02-20 Maya Patel (Eng): Concern about animation cost on low-end clients; requested static affordance fallback and performance budget of <12ms frame on route open.

2026-02-25 Olivia Chen (Research): Usability test plan in place — recruiting 10 participants (mix of infra engineers & PMs), tasks include 'locate rollout for model beta' and 'switch workspace to staging'.

2026-03-03 Ava Nguyen (Design): Prototype v2 uploaded. Reduced primary lanes, introduced 'context lanes' grouping (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost & Billing, Models). Added mini-preview on hover for rollout state.
2026-03-08 Miguel Alvarez (Design): Accessibility review — ensured collapsed labels have aria-labels and focusable mini-actions. Added contrast checks for compressed icon states.
2026-03-10 Diego Ramos (PM): Approved direction for MVP. Next: engineering refinement sprint for runtime + telemetry.

notes: Trade-offs: we favor discoverability for intermediate users over absolute minimal chrome for expert users. Follow-up ticket will evaluate 'compact expert mode' if telemetry shows >20% expert usage. Engineering flagged RBAC for workspace switcher as a blocker for multi-tenant rollout; schedule sync with Security on 2026-03-12.
